{{short description|Lifts an action of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra on a manifold to a Lie group action}}
In [[differential geometry]], a field of mathematics, the '''Lie–Palais theorem''' is a partial converse to the fact that any [[Lie group action|smooth action]] of a [[Lie group]] induces an infinitesimal action of its [[Lie algebra]]. {{harvs|txt|last=Palais|year=1957|authorlink=Richard Palais}} proved it as a global form of an earlier local theorem due to [[Sophus Lie]].

== Statement ==
Let <math>\mathfrak{g}</math> be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra and <math>M</math> a [[closed manifold]], i.e. a [[Compact space|compact]] [[Differentiable manifold|smooth manifold without boundary]]. Then any infinitesimal action <math>a: \mathfrak{g} \to \mathfrak{X}(M)</math> of <math>\mathfrak{g}</math> on <math>M</math> can be integrated to a smooth action of a finite-dimensional Lie group <math>G</math>, i.e. there is a smooth action <math>\Phi: G \times M \to M</math> such that <math>a (\alpha) = d_e \Phi (\cdot,x) (\alpha)</math> for every <math>\alpha \in \mathfrak{g}</math>.

If <math>M</math> is a [[manifold with boundary]], the statement holds true if the action <math>a</math> preserves the boundary; in other words, the vector fields on the boundary must be tangent to the boundary.

== Counterexamples ==
The example of the [[vector field]] <math>d/dx</math> on the open [[unit interval]] shows that the result is false for non-compact manifolds.

Similarly, without the assumption that the Lie algebra is finite-dimensional, the result can be false. {{harvtxt|Milnor|1984|loc=p. 1048}} gives the following example due to Omori: consider the Lie algebra <math>\mathfrak{g}</math> of vector fields of the form <math>f(x,y) \partial/\partial x + g(x,y) \partial/\partial y</math> acting on the torus <math>M = \mathbb{R}^2/\mathbb{Z}^2</math> such that <math>g (x,y) = 0</math> for <math>0 \leq x \leq 1/2</math>. This Lie algebra is not the Lie algebra of any group.

== Infinite-dimensional generalization ==
{{harvtxt|Pestov|1995}} gives an infinite-dimensional generalization of the Lie–Palais theorem for Banach–Lie algebras with finite-dimensional [[Center of a Lie algebra|center]].
